job: Designing a mid-execution human-input primitive so a running tool can suspend the agent, ask a typed question, and resume after restart.
outcome: A documented suspend-ask-resume checkpoint in the coding agent that persists paused state and survives a full process or server restart.
motivation: Unattended long-running agents risk wrong irreversible actions; a durable pause-and-ask control surface prevents them and differentiates the product.

task.where: the agent runtime's tool-call and session layer
task.when: the runway from June 2026 through H1 2027
task.why: to stop irreversible unattended actions taken without human intervention

job: Extending the framework's human-in-the-loop signal so a paused agent step holds typed operator input as durable workflow state across restarts.
outcome: A documented human-input checkpoint where a running step suspends, requests approval or a typed answer, and resumes the same run after restart.
motivation: Durable-execution runtimes already converge on orchestration-side checkpoints; a tool-level ask-user primitive completes their human-in-the-loop story.

task.what: Add typed suspend-ask-resume signal to durable steps
task.where: the workflow durability and signaling layer
task.when: the runway from June 2026 through H1 2027
task.why: to hold human approval as persisted state, not re-prompts

job: Shipping a documented mid-execution human-input feature so platform-hosted agents can pause for operator approval and resume after a server restart.
outcome: A named, documented restart-durable approval primitive in the managed agent service, distinct from transient prompts or pre-run allowlists.
motivation: Enterprise customers moving agents into unattended production demand auditable, restart-safe human approval gates before irreversible actions execute.

task.where: the managed agent runtime and control plane
task.when: the runway from June 2026 through H1 2027
task.why: to give enterprises restart-safe approval gates for production agents
